reviews.text: Unfortunately, I would not revisit a Melia resort. My original reservation was in Mexico, our family was switched to Punta Cana due to the cartel killing and the increase in violence in Mexico our president suggested for US citizens to avoid traveling to Mexico , the Melia resort would not honor a transfer to Punta Cana resort.  So unfortunately we paid double so we could join our family reunion. The resort is beautiful, the service was hit or miss. Some employees went above and beyond  i.e. Angelo and a another female employee I forgot her name but work at the Fahrenheit 90 pool the week of 6/17/26 was super attentive and accommodating our entire family at the pool bar, Annagracie at the Nick’s,  Kelvin our concierge did his best to accommodate our needs,  Jose at Santi treated us fabulously, Luis at the Mexican restaurant did a great job.  The only bad apple was  Magda at Kick’s could have been a little more kind and treated  us a little more respect. I’m hoping the day she served us she was only having a bad day. But we spoke to other guest and they also had a bad experience with her. The water system in the rooms was poor, no pressure, no hot water at peak times morning and evenings. The food was good.  I was very upset seeing and hearing children crying at dinner at an all inclusive  Adult resort. It was difficult getting restaurant reservations especially when you first arrive, trying to get ride from the airport through the resort was impossible. We could not get anyone on the phone and no emails returned in regards to transportation. We ended up taking our chances with a taxi. We loved the beauty of the hotel but will probably not return.

reviews.text:
_Excellent structure, but falls short in three areas_

Positive points: The resort is beautiful and very well maintained. The pools and beach are excellent. The staff's service deserves special mention; everyone is super attentive and helpful. The quality of the food and drinks is also above average for all-inclusive resorts in the region.

Negative points: I missed having a games room. Another point that bothered me was the difficulty of accessing some services, especially the themed restaurants. Without hiring a concierge, the available hours are very inconvenient and you are quite limited. There was also a charge before check-in, even though the reservation stated that payment would not be in advance. This caused confusion.

Would I return? Yes, for the structure and service. But I would only recommend hiring a concierge and confirming the payment conditions directly with the hotel to avoid surprises.

reviews.author: Michael Marcovich
reviews.text:
We are staying at the Paradisus Palma Real and Flora is an amazing restaurant! Such friendly staff, fast service and amazing food! The steak, the short rib and pretty much all the appetizers are beyond amazing. My friends and I were so happy with all the food including the dessert. Our server was super friendly and was accommodating to us.

100% recommend.

Update:

I am very bewildered. I wrote a review directly to the company, but I don’t recall posting anything on Google. This is very very odd. Anyhow. I remember writing that I loved Flora, but also spoke about all the negative things about this place that outweighed the positives.

First off, the “Reserve” was not worth the additional money. You don’t really get better service. If you book via Expedia, then you get slightly better service. The rooms were mediocre.

The shower had some workmanship issues. The water in the shower flowed away from the drain, causing floors to always be wet with an inch of water. The tv was working on a few channels with only some quality on sound and picture. The room said “swim up” but you needed to walk out of the room down a stretch to get to the pool, not right off your porch. The mini bar had a few cokes, a few small beers and a few waters, no liquor. I have done these type of resort rooms and this was not normal to me.

Staff: if you read above, it says I wrote friendly staff. There were very few who were friendly, most ignored your requests or just didn’t make you as a guest a priority. The front desk had no smaller change cash to tip your staff and the ATM was broken. I had to go to the casino at the other resort to get smaller change. Overall, the staff were pretty bad, especially at the restaurants!

The food and drinks:

Mostly terrible. The Reserve bar, at Silva had good drinks, but everywhere else, either Ehh, or bad. Also limited alcoholic choices too.
The food as I said, but didn’t say, at Flora, was good. It wasn’t amazing, but it was good! Everywhere else was pretty crap. My brother got pretty sick and couldn’t poop straight for weeks. I actually had to send back my dish at the steak restaurant because it was inedible. The Italian was pretty bad too, some good dishes, but I could have cooked better pasta dishes at home.
The Mexican restaurant was all around bad and charges for top shelf tequila as expensive add on’s.

The beach was great! The only issue is the constant solicitations when you just want to relax and this one person insisted on giving me a pedicure and I have very nice feet and toes comparably, and they did an absolute botched job and try and charge me more than a 1 hour pedi in the US for only 15 minutes at the beach.

Overall do not recommend. Felt a waste of money. Oh and lastly they don’t honor the “spa discounts” you get when you book the trip through whoever you get it from and tell you that their inclusive discounts supersede the ones you get, so really you pay 200+ dollars for an hour message. With no discounts.

reviews.text: The resort itself is beautiful. The beach is kept clean. The food was really good at the restaurants and the buffet. However all of this was negated because this property has roaches. Not large water bugs but actual roaches 🪳🪳🪳🪳🪳. I saw another review showing this and should have viewed it before staying. We were so paranoid we would bring back roaches with us we shook everything out before leaving the property. We addressed it with the front desk who then directed us to guest services. All they did was have the room cleaned again and sprayed. No compensation. We emailed their customer care team after the trip. They first needed proof which thankfully we took a video and photo of the first roach we saw. They then said there was no record of the incident at the hotel and denied any compensation since in their words this is typical for tropical places. Untrue I’ve never encountered roaches in any resort I’ve stayed at! They then researched more and found I did report the incident but said my reservation was under some type of complimentary stay. I then said this is false I paid nearly $4000 for my 2 rooms and at this point I feel like you all are making up excuses to not compensate me. They then came back and said sorry again you are correct. There final decision was to give me an upgrade for a future reservation. If you think I will ever stay at another Melia property you are sadly mistaken! This was the first and absolutely the last time! This brand is not trustworthy. Nobody spends thousands to share a room with roaches! This site won’t allow me to upload my video unfortunately.

reviews.author: Kuhananth Karuna
reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real was nothing short of amazing! From the moment we arrived, the staff welcomed us with genuine warmth and made us feel like valued guests. The resort is absolutely stunning, with beautiful tropical landscaping, pristine pools, and direct access to a breathtaking white-sand beach with crystal-clear turquoise water.

The room was spacious, spotless, and beautifully designed, offering a perfect blend of luxury and comfort. Every detail, from the comfortable bed to the balcony views, made our stay even more relaxing.

The food exceeded our expectations. With multiple restaurants offering a variety of cuisines, every meal was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The buffet had an excellent selection, and the specialty restaurants delivered an outstanding dining experience. The bars served delicious cocktails, and the service was consistently friendly and attentive.

The entertainment and activities kept us busy throughout the day and evening. Whether relaxing by the pool, enjoying the beach, or watching the nightly shows, there was always something fun to do. The resort was clean, well-maintained, and offered a peaceful yet lively atmosphere.

What truly made this vacation unforgettable was the exceptional hospitality. Every staff member we encountered went above and beyond to ensure we had a wonderful experience. Their professionalism, kindness, and attention to detail made us feel at home.

If you’re looking for a luxurious all-inclusive getaway in Punta Cana with outstanding service, delicious food, beautiful accommodations, and a spectacular beach, Paradisus Palma Real is an excellent choice. We left with incredible memories and are already looking forward to returning. Highly recommended for couples, families, and anyone seeking a relaxing five-star Caribbean vacation!

reviews.text:
Excellent experience at Blue Agave inside the Paradisus Punta Cana. My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed the Mexican food. We ordered the enchiladas and the tacos al pastor, and both dishes were delicious, full of flavor, and very well prepared.

As an appetizer, we tried the ceviche, which was fresh and perfectly seasoned. To finish, we shared the churros for dessert, accompanied by an exquisite chocolate sauce for dipping, which was the perfect ending to the meal.

We also want to highlight Lorena, our hostess, who made our experience even more enjoyable. From the moment we arrived, she was very kind, professional, and attentive, making sure we were comfortable and that everything went perfectly. Her warmth and excellent customer service truly made all the difference.

The service was excellent, and the restaurant's ambiance perfectly complemented the experience. We definitely recommend Blue Agave to anyone visiting the resort who wants to enjoy authentic, high-quality Mexican food. We will definitely be back! reviews.author: Laura Thomas
reviews.text: I recently stayed here with my sister to celebrate my 50th birthday.  The resort is gated which made us feel safer and the grounds are beautiful and maintained daily.  We had an Oceanfront room in the reserve adult only section,  it was worth the extra money.  I loved waking up to the water view every morning.  We had our own concierge,  Harry,  who was amazing! The food was good, nothing exceptional but good. We were not impressed with the restaurant that was only for the guests staying at the reserve, we both agreed that the other restaurants were better.  The resort is large and we never felt like it was overcrowded. The pools are beautiful and they maintain the beach. It's more of a quieter resort,  so if you are looking for something that has a lot of activities,  this is not the place for you. They do have a few daily activities but not much. Everyone we encountered that worked at the resort was so nice and helpful.  Fernando,  who i believe ia the activities director,  was very fun and personable.  I highly recommend this resort if you are looking for a place to unwind.

The hotel grounds are beautiful and well maintained.

In general, the beach, restaurants, and pools are gorgeous. Surprisingly, the buffet was amazing for all meals. We especially enjoyed the dinner specials.

If you are a Club Melia member, they are phasing us out. reviews.author: Anny Nunez
reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real Punta Cana completely exceeded our expectations and honestly became one of our favorite vacations. We stayed in The Reserve section and from the moment we arrived, the check-in process was effortless and set the tone for the rest of our trip.

I want to recognize Jose, our bellman, who was exceptional from the moment we arrived until the day we left. He welcomed us with kindness, was always helpful, and made sure our arrival and departure felt smooth and stress free.

I also want to recognize our concierge, Christopher Rivera (Chris) because he truly made this vacation unforgettable. He was attentive, professional, kind, and arranged every dinner reservation, checked on us constantly, made sure we had everything we needed. For my birthday dinner, he worked with my husband to organize a private dinner on the beach, complete with a speaker playing a special song. It was honestly one of those moments that felt like a dream. The level of care and attention he gave us is something you usually only find at truly exceptional luxury properties.

Special recognition also goes to Arismendi, who served us during my birthday dinner and completely elevated the experience. He spelled my name on the beach with lights, he took photos, recorded videos, helped us pose, and genuinely seemed excited to make our night special.

Dilania at the pool area was wonderful and constantly checked on us to see if we needed drinks or anything else. I really enjoyed her company.

Rafael at the beach area absolutely deserves special recognition because he consistently went above and beyond every single day. He somehow managed to always appear at the perfect time asking if we needed anything. He was friendly, professional, genuinely warm, and made every interaction feel personal rather than transactional. Whether it was helping us get comfortable, finding things we needed, or simply making sure we were enjoying ourselves, Rafael constantly exceeded expectations.
Carlos made my special birthday drink and Gladys gave one of the most relaxing massages I've had. The reality is there are too many wonderful people to name because from housekeeping to the coffee shop employees, buffet staff, gift shop staff, sports bar staff — everyone was exceptional.

Our beachfront walkout room was absolutely worth it. We had what felt like the perfect room with every amenity you could think of: slippers, razors, toothbrushes, fully stocked minibar, and all the small details that make luxury resorts feel luxurious.
The resort itself is beautiful, spacious, clean, and feels upscale without feeling pretentious. There were always plenty of beach chairs and cabanas available, multiple pools to choose from, and the beach itself was clean and beautiful.

Now for the brutally honest part: we travel often and have a pretty discerning palate, so food is usually where we are hardest to impress. The buffet had a huge variety and something for everyone. I absolutely loved that they served authentic Dominican breakfast with mangú, salami, and fried cheese. The omelet station deserves recognition too because that chef was phenomenal. Our favorite restaurants were Kanna Asian (the hibachi was excellent), the steakhouse, and the Italian restaurant.

The drinks were exactly what I expected from an all-inclusive resort: good, fun, but not necessarily craft cocktail quality. If you travel all-inclusive often, you already know what to expect.

The resort offers plenty of activities during the day and the nightly shows were decent, but one thing worth mentioning is that nightlife is limited. Once the shows end around 11 PM, the sports bar is pretty much your late-night option.

Overall, this resort gave us luxury, relaxation, incredible service, and memories that we will probably talk about for years. We arrived as guests and genuinely left feeling like family. Would absolutely return.

reviews.text:
The resort is a 10/10. The employees, every single one of them, from hostess, to bartenders, to housekeepers, to concierge, make the resort a 2/10.

This would’ve been a very pleasant vacation at an amazing property, but the employees make sure to not make you feel welcomed. The only guy that was welcoming was Miguel the bartender at the Rum bar. He gave us a smile, had the most positive vibe and was just great. I should also add that Patricia and Eva from the spa were amazing when providing their services.

Our “concierge” Adriel, never gave us a tour to the property. We had to walk to our room by ourselves after waiting for over an hour at the reception desk where he never showed up. We were told we would text us, he never did. I had to go out of my way and find a way to contact him.

If you’re not +50 and white, don’t expect good treatment. If you’re a young couple in your 20s, expect nothing but absolutely nothing. Mind you we came with the American Express program and had access to the Reserve. That meant nothing apparently. We waited over 30min to be brought a Diet Coke to Santé which is the “reserve” restaurant, but all three servers were too busy serving one table with 3 Americans, so we got up and left and instead, went to the general buffet at the other side of the property.

I would absolutely love to come back, and bring my mother, siblings and my wife again, but with the level of service from the employees, I don’t know if I want to swipe my card at this place again.

Employees here need to be trained on customer service. And be taught that a young couple is also capable and has the same resources as an older couple in their 50s. Times have changed. Start paying respect to younger people who also pay every single dime to be here.

reviews.author: Bernardo Huyke
reviews.text:
Overall, the hotel is a luxurious, beautiful resort with very good facilities. The beaches and pools are also very good for those who want to relax and enjoy the sun and heat. The spa is excellent for relaxation with very professional service.

Now, what really leaves something to be desired is the food:

1) Breakfast: Score 9/10
Overall, everything was very good and there were good options. However, I believe that the items prepared for consumption should be changed more frequently (fresher) due to the heat and possible contact with insects. The coffee could also be left in a specific place where people can serve themselves without having to wait for the waiter to bring it. Many times it took a long time or the coffee even arrived cold.

2) Buffet Lunch: Score 2/10

Lunch was, I believe, the weakest point of our entire experience. Considering that we were in a 5-star resort, the minimum expected was well-seasoned, fresh food with healthy options as well. However, it was the opposite. The food, after a certain time, isn't replaced until it runs out. If it doesn't run out, they won't replace it. The taste is that of a regular restaurant, something you could eat anywhere, not at a resort. Finally, the options tended to be more fried and junk food than a healthy option if you wanted one.

3) Dinner at the themed restaurants: Score 8/10

Overall, the food is very good. However, the service could be more consistent. Sometimes we had a very helpful and kind waiter, other times it seemed like the person was lazy or unwilling to serve. Another suggestion: the Dominican restaurant (local food) needs to improve its menu; the food was bland. As for the steakhouse, the seasoning was very good, but the meat arrived extremely cold. The question that needs to be answered is: why do they leave the meat waiting so long after it's cooked? It's unacceptable to eat cold roast beef…

4) Room Service: Rating 0/10

Speechless. Besides waiting for more than 2 hours, the food arrived extremely cold and inedible. This is unacceptable for a resort.

5) Snacks and Lunch Food

There was the Kicks bar which was very good, but it was the only place where you could find smaller meals or appetizers. I believe they should have more of this type spread throughout the resort. Sometimes people don't want to eat at the buffet. They simply want to order some fries and chicken wings, something small and not far from the pools or the beach.

Once I asked near the beach, they told me I had to call room service or go to the buffet. Which also doesn't make much sense.

reviews.author: Jenna Grounds
reviews.text:
My stay at Paradisus Palma Real was absolutely wonderful and exceeded my expectations. This was the perfect destination for a long vacation, offering a beautiful balance of relaxation, luxury, and exceptional service from beginning to end.

The resort grounds are stunning, meticulously maintained, and create a peaceful tropical atmosphere that makes it easy to unwind. One of the things I appreciated most was how spacious and comfortable the rooms were. The accommodations felt luxurious and thoughtfully designed, with plenty of room to relax. The room was well equipped with everything I needed throughout my stay, making it feel like a home away from home. The beach doesn’t have sargassum as it is cleaned throughout the day and there is a barrier.

The food was consistently excellent across the resort. The hibachi restaurant was one of the highlights of my trip, and Eddy made the experience especially memorable with his great energy and entertaining performance. I also thoroughly enjoyed the Mexican restaurant and the steakhouse, both of which served delicious meals with excellent service. There was a great variety of dining options available, and I always found something enjoyable to eat.

What truly made this vacation special was the incredible staff. A huge thank you to my concierge, Yaleidi, who went above and beyond to ensure that my stay was enjoyable and stress free. Yaleidi was attentive, responsive, and always willing to help with any request. I would also like to recognize Laura, the supervisor, who worked alongside my concierge to make sure I had the best possible experience. Her professionalism and dedication to guest satisfaction did not go unnoticed. Christian was another concierge who was incredibly helpful, friendly, and welcoming throughout my stay as he is easy to locate. Also - Gustavo made sure any little thing I needed was taken care of and checked on me throughout the day. (You can always find him)

The level of hospitality provided by the team made me feel genuinely valued as a guest. Everyone I interacted with was kind, professional, and committed to creating a memorable experience. The service, accommodations, dining, and overall atmosphere all came together to create an unforgettable vacation. Rafael at the beach bar is the absolute BEST!!

I would highly recommend Paradisus Palma Real to anyone looking for a luxury all inclusive resort in Punta Cana. Whether you are visiting for a romantic getaway, a family vacation, or simply a chance to relax and recharge, this resort delivers an exceptional experience. I look forward to returning in the future. If you are an adult, I 100000% recommended upgrading to the reserve because of the value and benefits.

Oh, also the destination inclusive activity was amazing!

Ultimately, they ended up giving me two towels. I went back to my chairs and the lady that I asked for the towels did nothing to replenish the towels at that station. She was more concerned with playing on her phone than helping any vacationer.

This is one example of many experiences. I was paying for A total of three rooms which equates to just under $15,000 for this vacation, including airfare. Next year, I will take that money and go to Resort that welcomes me.

This is very sad because this was our favorite place to vacation.

I strongly encourage everyone to read the reviews before you spend your money here. If service is important to you, this is not the place to come.

reviews.author: Amanda Wontor
reviews.text: The staff here has been wonderful. Servers, bartenders, hostesses - everyone has been polite and welcoming. Daniela at Mascalzone was especially great. She was able to seat us 2hrs earlier than our reservation so our almost 2yr old, who was exhausted after a day of swimming, could have dinner before he fell asleep. She treated him (and us) with kindness, giving him a high-five and crayons and was very sweet. The food was great, too! Our server, Yuleni provided top-notch service! Jean at Flora was awesome, too. Our son slept through dinner, so we asked for a cup of milk to bring back to the room for when he woke up.  He gave us a whole milk container. We felt like our son has been a priority for the staff here, which is really great to see at a resort that primarily caters to adults. Jeremy and Luis at Ginger (hotel lobby bar and coffee bar) were fun to hang out with while we ordered a few drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic - craft cocktails with plenty of options, including fruit juices and smoothies). They make great mojitos and espresso martinis! Overall, we highly recommend this resort, especially for families with very little ones who love to swim (and try new food!).

reviews.author: Cristina Tina
reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 4/5 – Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort

We had a really great experience at Paradisus Palma Real and it’s definitely the kind of resort where you have so many facilities and activities that you never feel the need to leave the property.

The hotel was very clean, and the WiFi was surprisingly amazing — it worked perfectly even on the beach, which is pretty rare for such a large resort. We also got a complimentary room upgrade, which made the start of our vacation even better 😊

The food was diverse and tasty: fish, seafood, sushi every day, lots of fresh fruit, and different meat options cooked to your preference.( thank you Edisson and Jimbert). The included drinks were also varied and good — wine, beer, Aperol Spritz, Cuba Libre, Margarita, Piña Colada, and more.

The resort is divided into 3 sections: adults only, family, and VIP, each with different wristbands and some restaurants/facilities with restricted access. There were a few places we couldn’t access depending on the bracelet category, but honestly we didn’t really feel limited because there were still plenty of restaurants, pools, and bars available to us.

The pools are a huge plus — basically every accommodation area has its own pool, plus one massive main pool. There’s always something happening and it’s impossible to get bored. They also have a coffee shop, sports bar, and live shows/concerts every evening

The beach was also beautiful, clean, and very well maintained, with gorgeous turquoise water and plenty of space to relax . The only downside was the slightly annoying “sunbed reservation culture” — many guests would leave towels or personal items on loungers very early in the morning to keep them occupied for hours, even when nobody was actually there.

Overall, a really good all-inclusive resort for relaxation, fun, and variety. Big like 👍

reviews.text:
The perfect place for a carefree getaway.

The hotel is located on a very large property, which includes several Melia hotels. The price includes on-site attractions at the Fun Republic complex, including a rope park and mini golf. The Rafa Nadal Tennis Center, a tennis and paddle tennis court complex, is available for an additional fee. Transportation within the area is very efficient thanks to electric scooters.

The food in the main restaurant is varied and constantly replenished.

Dinner reservations at themed restaurants, including Italian, Asian, and steakhouses, are available as part of your stay. Some restaurants are adults-only.

The hotel staff is very polite and helpful, not pushy about tips, which are, however, encouraged and appreciated.

If I had to point out any downsides, it would be the irregular room cleaning. Sometimes in the morning, sometimes during the day, and sometimes in the evening. This was a bit of a nuisance.

And the lounger by the room was dirty upon arrival and looked the same upon arrival – it hadn't been cleaned. But these are really just minor problems in paradise:)

reviews.author: Aitor G
reviews.text:
The hotel is adequate for a beach resort in the Dominican Republic, but it falls far short of the standard Meliá Hotels International sets for a 5-star hotel with The Reserve category within Paradisus.
Upon arrival, although they insisted we were assigned a superior room, the reality is that we weren't: it's the most basic suite. We are Meliá Platinum members, which implies a certain loyalty to the chain in exchange for privileges that were not honored here. They gave us The Reserve wristband, but the room is at the opposite end of the hotel from that area. They claim the hotel is full, but that's not true: even the staff themselves mention that the low season is starting and they are sending staff home.
We tried to make a reservation at one of the six available restaurants, but they directed us to the one they chose because "the others are full." That's not true either: there were clearly empty tables. The constant feeling is that they direct you according to their convenience, not according to actual availability.
From the second day onwards, you begin to notice a lack of quality in basic details. At the buffets, for example, there's a clear shortage of serving tongs: just one for several items (cold cuts, salmon, etc.), which poses a problem for allergy sufferers. Cleanliness also leaves much to be desired; our sheets weren't changed in four days. The Japanese restaurant is particularly poor, inferior to budget buffets in Spain. At the other restaurants, if you go where they suggest, the wait between courses is excessive (20 minutes between the starter and main course).
Getting towels at some of the kiosks is simply impossible: they tell you there aren't any and offer no alternative. At a resort of this caliber, running out of towels and not offering a solution is unacceptable.

Another example of disorganization: I rented a car and provided the driver's information and license plate number beforehand so they could access the lobby and finalize the rental agreement. The next day, they blocked the driver's entrance and forced me to complete the process standing at the door, after being transported in a trolley. Only after calling customer service was the issue resolved.

On our last day, despite being Platinum guests, we were initially denied a two-hour late check-out, with the explanation that they were full. After expressing our dissatisfaction, they changed their story: now it turns out our room is "special" because it connects to the one next door, and they need it. Coincidence or not, the adjoining room was occupied by a corporate group still staying at the hotel, with visible signage on the door. Finally, at 11:55, they granted us those two "complimentary" hours.
To top it all off, we witnessed a woman fall in the central plaza and remain on the ground for quite some time without any member of staff coming to her aid. This feeling of a lack of involvement is constant: what happens simply isn't their concern.
In short: it's not a bad hotel in absolute terms, but it falls far short of the standard one expects—and pays for—at a Paradisus The Reserve. If you arrive with those expectations, it's hard not to leave disappointed.

reviews.text: Now that I am back home, I wanted to take the time to talk about Paradisus Palma Real; I have been visiting this hotel for about three years now and I have never had a complaint; every time I go, the experience gets better, the food improves, and the overall atmosphere keeps evolving in a positive way; this time I went with my sister and my daughter, and honestly, if I had not come, I would have missed this new level of entertainment and energy; they have a staff member called Fernando Chispa who is truly outstanding and worth ten people in one; together with Jan, they form a perfect team within the entertainment group, and you can really feel the vibe and the unique spark that Fernando brings; the hotel is perfect, the staff is excellent, and I already feel like I want to go back again soon.

reviews.text: I stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real resort and my experience was simply unforgettable. From the moment you arrive, you're eager to return. The restaurants are spectacular, especially the Dominican restaurant: fresh, delicious food with an authentic flavor that makes all the difference. Plus, there are so many activities to enjoy every day, so you're never bored. I want to especially highlight the entertainment team, like Fernando Chispa and Henry, who were outstanding. Fernando Chispa, in particular, has it all: he not only radiates incredible energy but also teaches. reviews.author: Zarenna Porter
reviews.text:
My partner and I (from London) stayed at Paradisus Palma Real for 8 nights. First tip if it’s your first time in the DR: all the Meliá hotels sit in one large, beautifully curated compound. On arrival, we were genuinely impressed—it’s a stunning resort with a lot going for it.

We booked an adults-only king room but were initially given two doubles. Staff were polite, but we had to stay the first night and return in the morning to switch. Thankfully, that was sorted quickly. Overall, the resort caters well to couples, families, and groups.

One buffet plus 6 à la carte restaurants (more if you’re “Reserve” or “Circle”). Best meals were at Mina and Tokimeku. Huge thanks to Jean at Mina for standout service (and proactive second drinks—rare here). Mina had great food and atmosphere. Tokimeku was also excellent; we went twice. Special mention to Romeris, who runs Tokimeku and breakfast—warm, attentive, and a real asset.

The lowlights:

Flora: Supposedly Dominican cuisine. The “slider” was just meat in bread, and the goat dish was mostly fat and bones. Also experienced possibly the worst passionfruit mojito ever—medicinal, with tired mint and poor technique.

Blue Agave: Fish tacos arrived raw (not in a trendy sushi way). Surprisingly little concern when we pointed it out. However, the al pastor tacos were excellent. Churros were stale. A mixed bag, but raw fish is a bold choice.

Mascalzone: Americanised Italian. Starters were good, but mains arrived while we were still eating and were dumped on top of our plates. Pizza lacked spice; pasta was a bright orange cheese sludge. My partner refused it after two bites. Tiramisu was… not tiramisu. 2/10 unless you fear authentic Italian food.

Daily breakfasts and most lunches here. Some undercooked food early on led us to stick to safer options, which isn’t ideal on holiday. That said, good variety overall. Omelette station (especially Leudy) was a highlight.

The Winery: Best dining experience. You buy a bottle of wine and can order from any restaurant menu (default is Mina). Great ambience, excellent service from Jonathan, and a proper date-night feel. 9/10.

Service: Mixed overall. Standouts include Dilania at the adults-only pool—genuinely joyful and fantastic—and the bar team at Celsius. Rum Republic also great for evening drinks. Buffet service needs structure; often delays for cutlery or table clearing. Also, there seemed to be increasing pressure for reviews as the week went on.

Spa: Expensive for what it is. Even with a discount, a massage was ~£105—more than London prices without the quality jump. Also not particularly relaxing when the “silent” spa has loud groups. Nice setting, but not worth it.

Housekeeping: 5/10. Not dirty, but lacked attention to detail—mirror not cleaned, bedding questionable, items cleaned around rather than properly reset. Missing that 5* polish.

Other: On-site shop is very expensive. ATM charges ~4.5%. Tipping is expected ($1–$5 typical).

Overall: We enjoyed the holiday, the weather, and the people. The hotel feels like it’s hovering between 4* and 5*—great in parts, inconsistent in others. If true 5* service is reserved for premium members, the general offering probably leans closer to a 4*.

reviews.author: Dede C
reviews.text:
My partner and I have seen quite a bit of the world and will see more, but we won't be staying at a Melia again after this experience.

We booked through the website (where a fantastic room was advertised), but then came the shock when we saw the room. The picture and reality were two completely different things – opening the balcony door revealed a strong smell of a deep fryer. At night, it was so noisy (a fan outside the hotel room) that we couldn't really sleep.

We went to reception and explained that we hadn't booked this room and that we were dissatisfied. We were then told that there were no other rooms available. Friendliness and helpfulness were nonexistent.

We then showed the receptionist that our Melia app showed plenty of rooms available – the response: that was a false display.

Even if this were true and the entire hotel was fully booked, we would have at least expected some friendliness. It was clear that the staff didn't care at all and couldn't have cared less whether we were happy or not.


We were told that we weren't happy or helpful. There are restaurants, but they're booked up 3-5 days in advance – so the noisy cafeteria is the only option.

The beach is the best thing about the hotel. The staff there aren't exactly friendly, but at least the beach is beautiful.

There were sun loungers (already quite old), but the nice ones shown on the website are, of course, only available at an extra cost. Around us were people with coconuts (also featured in the hotel photos) – when you ask the staff, half of them know nothing about the coconuts, and the other half charge between $5 and $10 (in US dollars) for one.

We've never experienced such service before.

This was the first time we've ever left a hotel early and booked a different one.

Even though we have many years ahead of us, we'll never set foot in a Melia again.

reviews.author: Marcela R
reviews.text:
THE WORST HOTEL EXPERIENCE we've ever had. Belongings disappear and they keep your money.

My boyfriend and I went for our anniversary, and by the third day, I already wanted to go home.

We booked a room in the adults-only section, and when we arrived, they told us they didn't have any available. They tried to move us to a "better" room in the family area. We found a jacuzzi with mold and broken doors. We complained, and they sent us back to the adults-only section.

When we got to the room, it smelled damp. We complained again because I have asthma, and we both suffer from migraines, but they said they couldn't do anything. We wasted EVERYTHING on the first day because of all this. To avoid ruining the experience and hoping for better service, we decided to upgrade to The Reserve. THE WORST DECISION.

From the first day, the concierge didn't even come to greet us. We had to seek him out multiple times and constantly chase him down to get him to pay attention to our restaurant reservations and other inquiries. That "exclusive" experience they advertise is pure fiction.

On the third day, my boyfriend left some belongings on one of the beach lounge chairs while we went to breakfast (a stainless steel cup, a book, and some sandals), as he was told he could do early so we could have a peaceful breakfast. When we returned, the sandals had been moved, the cup had disappeared, and there were other people in the chairs. We complained, and security said they hadn't seen anything, nor had the waiters.

We were put in touch with Laura from guest services/supervisor who, after trying to blame us, finally agreed to look into how to help. They offered us a couple of experiences for our anniversary and a refund for the two nights of the upgrade we had paid for. This was on April 17th.

On both the 18th and 19th, we reiterated to her and the concierge that they should please leave the refund request at reception to avoid any problems. When we checked out, with our transportation waiting, they told us they knew nothing about it. We finally found her, and she told us it was already being processed and not to worry.

TO THIS DAY, WE HAVE NOT RECEIVED ANY PAYMENT, ANY REFUND, ANY MESSAGE ADVISING US OF WHAT HAPPENED. WHERE IS OUR MONEY? We have sent emails, called, even written to the concierge, and NO ONE has responded. I had to write this hoping that someone will deign to pay us.

In short, do not stay at this hotel if you are looking to relax, feel safe, have a good experience, and receive good customer service. The food is so bad that there were days we preferred not to eat. The rooms are very poorly cleaned. You have to ask for everything multiple times. Room service is nonexistent. The vast majority of the staff have a very bad attitude. The service is mediocre at best, and the only redeeming feature is the beach bar, which provided excellent service.

reviews.author: Stephanie Serra
reviews.text: One of the best sports bars we've visited. Great atmosphere, service, and music.

reviews.author: mike d
reviews.text:
There are pros and cons to this place, and I will list them accurately so that everyone can judge for themselves -
Pros - the place is located in a very beautiful area, the entire resort looks and feels like you're on vacation, and many of the pics you take will show very well, if its for social media posting or basic family pics,
The weather - depending on the time of year is usually great, you should be careful for excessive sun, the uv rating is extremely high, but understandably so,
Cons - I have been to this place 3 times over the past 20 years, and I remember when it 1st opened they had celebrities promoting it (JLo and the likes), and the service was absolutely amazing, where I had never experienced anything great like it before, that is why I chose to revisit more times, had a few family and friends do destination weddings here, and always highly recommend to everyone, but this last time I recently visited, I was let down and disappointed on so many levels that I don't see myself recovering from it, namely for these reasons -
I initially booked 5 rooms for a large family party, where their initial reservations told me I have to contact their corporate office because it was too much for them to handle, ok fine I did contact them, but trying to give them the down payment on my cc was a hassle because their company is based in Mexico and for some reason I had to reach out to my cc company where it still took 5 days to finally process, ok fine I received an email confirmation for the reservation booking,
Come to the arrival day, I come there with my family, coming off the bus and all ready to start our vacation, where I end up stuck at the front reception desk for 2 and half hours because they cannot locate or find my reservation, and they're looking at me like I’m from another planet, thankfully I showed them the email confirmation, to which they still had to locate us 5 rooms, to which I originally requested that we all be together within the same building area, but no, we ended up being spread all over the place separately, and they charged me for the entire cost without deducting the down payment, to which they kept telling me they could not locate it in their system, to which I kept showing them my email and cc statement where it showed that it was charged, starting off my vacation on this foot made me severely agitated and only further annoyed my entire time spent there,
I spent everyday at the front reception for a minimum of an hour trying to resolve and have the hotel locate and credit my deposit back to my card, only to be met with everyone ‘deeply apologizing’ to me and giving me their whatsapp phone numbers, but even when I texted anyone on their whatsapp, no one ever replied or answered me back the entire time, I demanded a meeting with the head person/manager/boss/whatever, where I got a phone call on the room phone only to have them keep saying “hello – hello, can you hear me?  Are you there?” and then only hung up.  Told this to the front desk and they said they would send someone immediately to change the phone in the room – which was not the problem.  I had to threaten them on the last day that I was going to dispute the entire charge on my credit card, to which then they miraculously found the down payment, and then proceeded to deduct it from the total amount charged.

reviews.text:
We had a fantastic time! My first trip to the Carribean and I'd say the bar has been set very high.

Staff for the most part was friendly and out going. People that complain about a particular staff member have to realize that these are humans with real emotions. I for one would be given horrible reviews for my personality but would otherwise give you fantastic service!

Food at the Lunch box buffet was by far our favorite. The no reservation times made it easier to eat when were actually hungry. We ate at Mina, Mascalzone and Blue Agave. All three were fantastic except I was disappointed by the steak I had at Mina. The NY Strip was tough as leather but tasted fine. I am just spoiled by eating Prime grade at restaurants in Canada, there's no way for an all inclusive in the DR can compete.

My only true complaint has nothing to due with the resort itself but the guests. We were up pre dawn most mornings to watch the sunrise (Spectacular!). We watched many guests place towels on loungers and beds and never come back to them, leaving those spots "reserved" and unused all day. We got our spots early and were in them all day by the beach or pool. Just disrespectful in my opinion.

You can tell that he loves what he does, always with a smile, motivating everyone and giving more than 100% at every moment. reviews.author: Alek Karpoff
reviews.text:
I’m currently staying at Paradisus Palma Real and overall, the experience has been very positive. The beach is beautiful, with wide, comfortable sun chairs that make it easy to fully relax. The property itself is spacious and well-maintained, and the rooms are large and comfortable. The restaurants have been a highlight - both the food and service are very good - and I’ve been especially impressed by the quality of the bar service and the drinks. Overall, we’re having a great time.

That said, there are a few downsides. The buffet has been the biggest disappointment: the food quality at lunch and dinner is not on par with the rest of the resort, and the lack of service there is noticeable - you have to find your own table and chase down drinks, which takes away from the experience. Similarly, there’s no real service on the beach. While staff are present, they seem to focus on serving “VIP” guests, leaving others without attention.

Another issue is the number of local vendors on the beach. There are a lot of them, and they approach frequently - every few minutes - which can become quite disruptive. Some are loud, playing videos or calling out, which makes it harder to relax and enjoy the setting.

Despite these drawbacks, it’s still a very good vacation spot overall. The positives outweigh the negatives, and I would come back.

My family and I stayed here last week, and the resort is extraordinary. The rooms are large, the pools are fantastic, there are several restaurants, and the buffet has a wide variety of delicious food. They also now have a play area similar to an amusement park for adults and children. Although there is sargassum on the beach, it's cleaned daily and is ideal for walking and enjoying the mornings. We enjoyed the activities, which cater to all tastes. In short, it's the perfect place to relax without having to leave the hotel.

It's worth mentioning that this place wouldn't be what it is without its wonderful people. There are many staff members, but I want to specifically mention the people who made our stay a 10/10: the lovely Luisa from the beach pool, Alberto from the pool bar, Natanael from security, Fernanda, Yanira, Milton, Jimbert, Frank, Hirlemne, Rosanna from the buffet, José and the bellhop staff, and our dear concierge, Wolfman. reviews.author: Stephanie Fanning
reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort was nothing short of exceptional. From the moment we arrived until the day we left, we were completely in awe of the beauty of the property - every morning felt like waking up in paradise.

While the resort itself is stunning, what truly made our experience unforgettable was the incredible support staff. Every single person we encountered was warm, attentive, and genuinely committed to making our stay special. In fact, we found ourselves keeping a list of the standout individuals who went above and beyond:

Melina (Flora) greeted us with such cheerfulness and  had fantastic recommendations that elevated our experience. (We're still talking about the appetizer she recommended)

Bernardo (Chauffeur) was effortlessly cool and personable - his energy set the tone for every interaction.

Jeyson (Beach Service) was attentive, funny, and by the end of the trip felt more like a friend than staff.

Cristal (Nespresso) was truly a bright light in our mornings - starting the day with her positivity made all the difference.

Margaret (Ginger) kept our drinks perfectly topped up and had us laughing every time she came by.

Edison (Lunch Box) was the definition of professionalism. He recognized us daily, checked in thoughtfully, and made sure our coffee and mimosas were always fresh.

Luis (Blue Agave) was an absolute highlight. His recommendations were spot-on, his energy was infectious, and he kept us laughing throughout the entire evening.

And finally, our hibachi team Felix, Maria, and Luis created such a memorable dining experience. Felix was a true character who brought our group together and made sure everyone felt included and well taken care of. The food was outstanding, and Maria and Luis ensured everything ran smoothly, from appetizers to drinks.

This team of people turned an already beautiful resort into a truly unforgettable experience. Their warmth, professionalism, and genuine care are what will bring us back again.

reviews.author: Manal Amara
reviews.text:
The truth is, the hotel is beautiful, and so is the beach; the location is perfect. However, what left a bad taste in our mouths during our stay was the management and the lack of friendliness from the staff. We would say hello and thank you, but on many occasions, they wouldn't even look at us or respond.

We booked with THE RESERVE option, which in theory offers more personalized service and a concierge who takes care of everything. Nothing could be further from the truth: we had to ask for things several times, and on several occasions, we arrived at restaurants where we supposedly had a reservation, only to find it wasn't there, so we had to go to the buffet. It's quite inconvenient and embarrassing to arrive thinking you have a table and be told that the reservation doesn't exist.

After complaining at reception, they started sending us confirmations, but we believe that these kinds of mistakes shouldn't happen in a hotel of this category.

The food is okay, but nothing remarkable for a 5-star resort like the Paradisus Meliá. Furthermore, we asked for non-alcoholic cocktails because we don't drink, and the staff didn't know how to make them, which is surprising in a hotel like this.

In short, the setting is incredible, but the service falls short. We left with mixed feelings because it didn't meet our expectations.

reviews.author: Tarah Fenn
reviews.text:
This one is going to hurt a little bit. I have several reviews to fill out including Delta Vacations. This was not an inexpensive vacation. We booked through Delta Vacations and flew from Phoenix to Atlanta to Punta Cana. Not a quick trip either.

Upon arrival, room was not ready. Took 2 hours for room to be ready. Front desk said we would get an email. We never got an email. Just hovered until they were tired of seeing us. NOTE: Your band on your wrist is an indicator of what you are getting there.

Rooms are decent. Although you will never get me to understand why a thin curtain is a good use of privacy over a wall or door. Doesn't matter who you are traveling with, you want privacy!

When you arrive at the hotel, you should be pulled aside by a concierge that you DO NOT HAVE TO PAY FOR to be informed about what your activities are and how to make dinner reservations. Don't get me started on that process. If you are a commoner---you will need to get in line at 8AM promptly by the buffet to TRY (operative word) to nab a dinner reservation. If you are unlucky at nailing a reservation, you win the BUFFET only. It's NOT ok to only have that option BUT that is the option. Food is MEH. The Italian place was my favorite. Tipping is weird. Some people leave a dollar; other people leave 20. I tried not to be a douche, but I did spend over $8K for this vacation so sometimes you get $5 and have to deal with it.

You should get a calendar of events, things that are available to use, marked areas where you can and can't go (trust me it matters)! The hospitality at this hotel is lacking. I can't tell you how many times people looked me dead in the eyes and ignored my question or request. I had to scour the entire hotel for 9 beach towels before my excursion and then I told the manager, keep an entire cart of them at the front of the bell desk for others. Cleaning services were amazing, bar tenders were subpar and often forgot drinks (even if you tipped them ahead of time). Buffet service was the WORST. Numerous requests for coffee go unnoticed. Trust me, I was nice and polite, and it did not matter. So I just stopped tipping at the buffet.

Also, I honestly don't believe the Dominican Republic understands the value of the American dollar whatsoever. It's one thing to pay $6 for a bag of skittles at the gift shop. It is another thing entirely to price a sweatshirt at $60 that is literally the same one on Amazon for $22.99 on prime. MANY of the places we visited were dramatically overpriced. They see you as a sucker and take advantage. They also expect your tips. They are TRAINED to not have change. I watched it happen and I also watched a taxi driver deliver money to a hotel and clearly was in cahoots with the souvenir shop. DO NOT GO TO THEIR SHOPS.

The major plus is the beaches! Of course they are stunning! The pools are great, the swim up bars and the liquor are great! Make sure to check out Fun Republic on property. No one told us about it until the last day but was fun for mini golf. Cabanas cost $160 a day and that is why they are always empty. No one is paying that (again an overpriced dollar thing). Another thing the resort should do is have a FREE cabana day. I mean they sit there and do nothing. It's literally crazy that they block the beach to make you PAY!! LOL.

Overall, I would not come back to this resort. This was NOT a 5-star experience!

I had a wonderful time because of the people that I was with. My family and friends are what made this trip spectacular. Even if my expectations were not met, my family created memories and enjoyed each other.

Signed---a green band girl in a brown band world (IYKYK). :)

reviews.author: Priyadarshini Manning

Celebrated my husband’s birthday at Mina Steakhouse and WOW…what an experience from start to finish. And the surprise birthday cake? What the heck…a cake!!! Such a thoughtful and memorable touch that made the night feel extra special. Seeing the biggest smile on my husband’s face said it all.

reviews.author: Zineb Benkirane
reviews.text:
We had an absolutely wonderful stay at Melia Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa and would highly recommend it.

The location is fantastic, with some of the most beautiful, soft white sand beaches and consistently gorgeous weather that made the entire experience feel like a true escape. The grounds are stunning—lush, green, and impeccably maintained, creating a serene and luxurious atmosphere throughout the resort. The standard rooms were very spacious and included a private balcony and sunbeds, with nice amenities and modern decor, with high quality marble flooring.

What really stood out, though, was the staff. Everyone was incredibly warm and welcoming, and the level of service was consistently on par. A special thank you to Jesus, Jose and the kind ladies at the kids’ club, who was especially kind, attentive, and with whom my children had a blast!

The breakfast buffet was very very nice with multiple options. We really appreciated that there à la carte restaurants included included our favorite Blue Agave, the Japanese and Italian, and the food across the board was very good, with an opportunity for improvement at Kanna lunch when the bbq meat was consistently undercooked. The lunch and dinner buffets, though good, were the same every day. The only small note would be the Hibachi Japanese restaurant—the chef didn’t include any of the usual entertainment, which would have made the experience even more enjoyable.

Another great perk was the sports amenities, including the top of the line gym that I enjoyed every morning and the Rafael Nadal Tennis Center, which added something unique and elevated to the stay.

Overall, this is a beautiful resort that delivers on quality, service, and atmosphere. We can’t wait to come back!

reviews.text:
I loved the location - right on the beach.  Super easy access to that.  Pool was a comfortable temperature and nice and clean.  Room was spacious and had lots of amenities that I was happy with.  Our room was a bit sandy when we checked in, but we're on the beach...so whatever.  Food was also pretty decent!  Lunch box had a wide variety of foods that my family and I enjoyed.  Mina was EXCELLENT.  We had room service one night and that was pretty darn amazing too.
The Nespresso cafe lady always had a smile on her face which was wonderful to see when compared to other unhappy faces.

Would I return?  No.
Service is subpar.  At a "5 star resort" I shouldn't be waiting 15min for coffee and that's IF I get coffee at all.  Literally we'd tell our server 2 coffees, they'd bring 1 empty cup.  Sometimes they'd fill that cup with coffee, sometimes they didn't.  Water refills were also infrequent - sometimes once during the entire meal.  Refills for other drinks we ordered were never offered.  Some of the staff have a smile and are understanding of the business of hospitality, most made us feel like they were purposefully ignoring us.  Just as an overall observation, you seem to get better service if you speak Spanish.
Yes we tipped everyone we interacted with and I always started the conversation with an hola and coma esta.  None of this seemed to help much in getting any attention from servers.
There were a few very lovely workers (all chefs at the lunch box are wonderful overall), but they're the exception and not the standard unfortunately.
The other annoyance that I encountered was at Blue Agave.  We had ordered a supplemental item, meaning an additional cost, which I was fine with and had it charged to the room.  When settling the bill, the waiter was "having difficulty" with the device and said that he would sign for us instead of having us wait for him to figure it out.  He didn't mention that he would also give himself an additional tip on top of the cash that we left him....It was only $1.50 USD so I let it go, but it's the principle and the audacity that is upsetting.  I mention this as a caution to the next person as maybe next time the additional tip won't be as small.

reviews.text:
Hotel is overrated. The price charged is completely unrealistic for what it offers. Upon arrival, the guy who took our luggage to the room left angry and slammed the door because he didn’t receive a tip. The room was supposed to be for a honeymoon from the start, but they gave us a room with two single beds and did not allow us to change it—unless we paid an extra U$$800.
There’s no coconut water, no freezers around the resort to grab drinks freely. There’s no ice cream. There’s no heated pool. It was hard to even find a bar that had food. You have to order food and wait for it to be prepared, sometimes taking more than 20 minutes. There’s no ice cream.
I tried to book a restaurant for dinner, but there was no availability—not even for the next day. And the restaurants don’t allow reservations more than two days in advance. I went to get a beer at the beach kiosk, and they said my reservation didn’t cover beach beer. I went to another bar to get wine, but the wines are extremely expensive (yes, they charge for wine at an “all-inclusive” resort).
The room amenities are low quality. Liquid soap. There’s no music, no parties, no shows. It claims to be adults-only, but there are lots of children. Food service is only available at certain hours at the buffet (the only place with food for those who couldn’t get restaurant reservations). I asked for a Corona at a bar, and they said I wasn’t entitled to it.
This is the worst all-inclusive resort I’ve ever been to. The price for this ? Almost U$$3.000 for 7 days and for my honeymoon!

reviews.text:
We recently stayed at Paradisus Palma Real – The Reserve, and while the property itself is beautiful, our overall experience didn’t quite live up to expectations.
The grounds are absolutely gorgeous and very well maintained—no complaints there. However, the service was inconsistent. Some staff members were warm, pleasant, and helpful, while others seemed inconvenienced and uninterested in assisting guests.
Dining was one of the biggest disappointments. Upon arrival, we were asked for our preferred restaurants, but when it came time to confirm reservations, none of our requests were available. We were left choosing between limited openings or the buffet. Food quality overall was underwhelming, including room service. The one highlight was the omelette bar, which was consistently good.
One bright spot of the trip was the main pool swim-up bar. The bartenders—Eddy, Jorge, and Dalania—were fantastic and truly made our last day enjoyable.
The room itself was another letdown. It felt very humid and never fully cooled, which made it uncomfortable at times. Additionally, our room wasn’t ready at check-in, and when we finally got access, the minibar hadn’t been stocked. While not a major issue on its own, it added to the overall feeling that the experience didn’t match the resort’s reputation.
We were honestly surprised by the high ratings, as we’ve had much better experiences at other Caribbean resorts. While the property looks incredible on paper, it didn’t deliver in several key areas.
Overall, not worth the hype.

reviews.text:
This hotel belongs to the same chain as the previous one where I stayed, but it's within the same complex. I first stayed at the other hotel and then moved to this one, which supposedly offered a higher category, specifically in the adults-only section.
My expectation was a better level of service, including perks like an exclusive beach and more personalized attention, but unfortunately, this wasn't the case. The exclusive beach service was never available.
Furthermore, this category includes concierge service, whose role is to assist guests and make their stay more enjoyable (reservations, recommendations, follow-up, etc.). In my case, the experience was very poor. The assigned concierge provided virtually no service: there was no follow-up, no interest, and no suggestions. He only made restaurant reservations. I even noticed a significant difference compared to other concierges who were very attentive to their guests. On my last day, he sent a farewell message, which I replied to, but I never received a response.
As for the hotel itself, it's an older structure, partially renovated, but it still feels like an old building. The room had a strong musty smell, which was quite unpleasant.
On the positive side, I must highlight the food, which was excellent in all the restaurants. The Italian restaurant, in particular, was outstanding.
For this reason, my rating is mixed: the food elevates the experience, but the service and the hotel's facilities fall short of expectations for this category.

reviews.author: Danyelis Zapata Beras
reviews.text: Excellent service from the very first moment. The place is very clean and well-maintained. All the staff were always friendly, attentive, and professional, making our stay truly pleasant. I could never finish mentioning all the staff who contributed to such a great experience. We stayed for seven days, and each day and each night the service was even better than the day before. Without a doubt, a place you'll want to return to—highly recommended! And a special mention must go to Fernando Chispa for his excellent service and the way he gets involved to ensure everything runs smoothly and that we have a great experience.

reviews.author: Dimanche Lucero
reviews.text: The Paradisus Palma resort is the best of the best. The food and service were incredible; the adults-only pool is spectacular, with impeccable service. We were treated wonderfully all week, served the best drinks, and created a fantastic atmosphere. The experience was excellent from beginning to end, and special mention must be made of Fernando Chispa for his excellent service, his ability to connect with people, and the way he contributes to the resort's ambiance.

reviews.author: Richard Packer
reviews.text:
Beautiful resort, excellent service.  Restaurants w great food, especially Blue Agave,
hostess Maria and Vertudes  were very accommodating.

reviews.author: audelina reynoso
reviews.text: I really enjoyed the Sport Bar, with its super friendly atmosphere, great service, and perfect spot to have a good time. The Ginger Bar was also an excellent experience, with expertly prepared drinks and a lovely ambiance. The entertainment team is amazing, always full of energy and making everything more fun; especially Fernando Chispa, who is the best because of his energy and dedication, along with Henry, who also brings a fantastic vibe.

reviews.author: Lucas Braja
reviews.text: Junior from Farahenheit bar the best bar tender and person at this resort - give him a raise he’s so good at what he does

reviews.author: Lisa Durocher
reviews.text: Reserve dinners were delicious with excellent service. We spent most days at the pool and the swim up bar service by Arisleida was top notch. Friendly and super at what she does. Took great care of us every day. She is an incredible and very hard worker.

reviews.author: angela rijo
reviews.text:
Every time I come to Paradisus Palma Real, I'm reminded that it's a truly unique experience. From the moment you arrive, everything feels elevated: the service is impeccable, the facilities are beautiful and meticulously maintained, and the food always surprises with its quality and variety. The ambiance is perfect for disconnecting and enjoying yourself, with a combination of tranquility, luxury, and positive energy that permeates every corner. But what truly makes the difference is the people. The entertainment team is incredible, always brimming with energy and making every day special. And without a doubt, Fernando "La Chispa" stands out for his charisma, his joy, and his talent for dancing. He's one of those people who radiates positive energy and makes the experience even more memorable.
Paradisus Palma Real isn't just a hotel; it's a place I always want to return to.

reviews.author: Sabrina K
reviews.text: Just stayed here over spring break and overall was a good time. The restaurants were good but the portions are very small. The service in most restaurants was good the service lacks a lot in the buffet which is understandable because of how crowded it gets but we’ve sat at tables that didn’t have glasses and/or silverware and it would take a long time to receive those also basic things like ketchup and salt would sometimes take a while to get to us (they mostly forgot and we had to remind them again) the beach and bar service was amazing we did a beach cabana multiple times and Yuderi was amazing, he set up the cabanas and lounge chairs with towels. got us drinks quickly and was overall a great guy and made it seamless process. Our room was great we had the master suite and it was beautiful, the housekeeping was so good and cleaned our room every day and gave us fresh towels. The one thing I will say is some workers really don’t speak good english and the language barrier can be very difficult when both sides don’t really understand each other. Overall had a good time and would stay here again. We did not have kids with us but there is a lot of stuff for kids to do there is the fun republic which we did not go to but seems very fun also it seems like every day there was a activity for kids they had a bunch of different inflatable things every day on the beach which was nice. They also had stuff at the pools like paddle boarding and other stuff. The pool was very clean and well kept. Also, I found multiple times that there is miscommunication throughout the resort. At the front desk we were told we can make a reservation at Olio. A new mediterranean restaurant. but when we went to the woman making the reservations she told us no. This was unfortunate because we were looking forward to that and had gotten told something different at the front desk was upsetting.

reviews.author: Lidiya Vynnytska
reviews.text:
Location and beach is the only nice thing about this place. They must have paid to people for the review here, otherwise I am not sure how someone would enjoy this place.
After 16 hours door to door travel from the UK we came here on 4th of April with the hope to finally have some rest. Instead I spent 3 hours back and forth with the front manager in duty trying to fit our family of 4 into room that has only one bed. She was absolutely unprofessional and lied to my face that they have no other rooms and that BA had sold us room with wrong description and we should deal with travel agent as they can’t do anything about it since their hotel in 100% capacity. Apparently junior suit with the separate living room and sofa bed meant to be in 1 room with the bench to sleep on as a sofa bed.
In addition we spent 2 days trying to have extra bed delivered to our room for my child.
Service in the main restaurant is appalling, they are lucking on all basic items every day, takes forever to get any drinks. (I would say there is no service). Rooms are generally not looked after.
We came to this hotel as they had golf and tennis, just so you know none is within the hotel and you need to pay extra to play it.
And highlight of the first day was when I came to the beach and they said they do not have any towels left🤬. Seriously, I had better service received in the 3 star hotels. This hotel charge you $550 per night as a 5*, however the place is generally mismanaged in every possible place. Would not recommend this place to anyone.

reviews.author: Christian Echevarria-Reina
reviews.text:
Total failure in customer service. We were trying to plan our wedding here but have since thought better of it.

We weren’t able to get ahold of the coordinator for wedding planning for weeks over email.

We were told by the general line that there were day passes and when we showed up security would not let us in to buy one. Turns out there is no such thing.

We called the general phone number and the person who answered was annoyed that we asked to be transferred to a number within the hotel.

When we finally spoke to the wedding department they put the blame on us for emailing what they said was a “general email” (there was not a specific email provided anywhere we could discern).

There seems to be a pervasive culture of finger pointing and bureaucracy in customer support where every person claims they are not in charge of X and that they do not know how to solve X.

It does not seem like they care very much about the customer experience.

reviews.author: Borja Ruiz
reviews.text: This is a note for Marta Actividades, who looked after our two children (ages 4 and 3). Marta was amazing, incredibly caring, attentive, and always willing to help. The children quickly warmed to her and would run off every day when they went to the kids' club. Highly recommended. Thank you so much, Marta!

reviews.author: Sasha Petty
reviews.text: We love it here! It’s our third time here. The activities are the best. Our daughter loves Kidsdom - yesterday they had the best Easter egg hunt and crafts. Martha at Kidsdom is just the sweetest and so welcoming. For adults, the pool classes (dance and fitness), mixology and art classes, and live music are amazing. Food has been really good (especially the restaurants) and the staff is the best. We will be back!!

reviews.author: olimpia sh
reviews.text: A fantastic family experience! Lots of activities for adults and children. The kids went to Kidsdom and loved it; Martha and Charlina were so attentive and caring with the children! We'll be back!

reviews.author: S U A P (Chamba)
reviews.text:
Excellent service from Ramoncito; he treated us like royalty on the beach. We must return for Christmas as well. We also had a great Easter vacation, spending the whole day at the beach with Ramoncito and enjoying top-notch drinks.
The rest of the restaurant staff are not at all friendly. If you ask them something, they answer rudely. There are very few employees who provide good service.

reviews.author: Plinio Julián Calvento
reviews.text: The hotel itself is excellent, but the overall service from the staff is poor. From the reception staff to the restaurant workers, the receptionists don't explain everything about the hotel properly, and the restaurant staff rush you to finish quickly. If you go during lunchtime or later, you always miss out on dessert. Friendliness and empathy are lacking; the staff needs more training. I would only mention the excellent service from Mr. Guillermo (the concierge), Mr. Gabriel, and the staff at Winnery.

reviews.author: Iñigo Goñi
reviews.text:
Our experience at this hotel was truly disappointing, especially regarding the check-in service. The process was extremely slow, disorganized, and unprofessional. We had the constant feeling that the staff were neither well-prepared nor knew how to handle the situation, which resulted in a long and unnecessary wait.

We are regular guests of the Meliá chain and are familiar with the level of quality they typically offer across their various brands, so this experience surprised us even more, and not in a good way. It's regrettable that something as basic as check-in becomes such a major problem. A simple inconvenience ends up turning into an interminable wait and a build-up of frustrations.

We hope that you will take steps to improve this aspect, as it directly affects the guest's first impression and falls far short of what one expects from this hotel group.
