reviews.text: It was my first time at a Meliá Paradisus hotel, and it exceeded my expectations. It's truly a top-tier luxury resort; all the services were impeccable, the food was delicious and varied, the service was superb at every turn, and the cleanliness and attention to detail are unbeatable. I must mention that "The Reserve" areas are well worth it; the tranquility is truly enjoyable. Just one observation: I was told my personal concierge would contact me during my stay, but that didn't happen. However, I must thank Maykol, the night receptionist, for his exceptional service. He helped me with everything I needed from the moment I arrived, showing me around the entire hotel, assisting me with my requests, and being attentive to my needs. He was my personal concierge, and he does a fantastic job. I hope to return soon, as there are many corners of the hotel I didn't get to explore. Thank you to the entire team.

reviews.author: Elena Favorido
reviews.text:
Beautiful facility overall, pools, beach access, restaurants. The highlight of our vacation was the activities' team and the many activities offered. Big shout out to Soranyi, Carlito, Freilyn, Jholfry and Jairo, great energy! The Dominican night was fun, but prepare to negotiate the prices if you plan to buy any souvenir..
Our room wasn't ready at the time of check-in and when we finally got in, there were still the ladies finishing up the beds. Some details were not on point for a 5 star resort, like a broken toilet seat, reading lamps not working, the safe buttons needed to be pushed super hard, the cleaning could be improved, the door had a gap and you could see the light and hear every noise from outside. We had to call the room service a few times as they missed stuff, like they took the shower mat and didn't replace it, or the tissues box was empty and didn't refill.. The staff would just randomly barge in the room for cleaning without knocking or ringing the bell.
Some of the waiters could use a smile, especially at the buffet, not impressed with the service. The food was good at the restaurants a la cart, but even with the rsvp we had long waiting time and missed a couple of night shows because of that. Lot of variety at the buffet but after sitting at room temperature for a while, some food didn't look safe to eat, like sushi, cheese and even fruit.

reviews.author: Christopher Jones
reviews.text:
Our dining experience at Kicks restaurant within the Paradisus Palma Real was absolutely phenomenal, largely thanks to the exceptional staff who truly made our evening memorable. From the moment we arrived, we were greeted with genuine warmth and attentiveness that set the tone for a fantastic meal.

Our server, Jose del Rosario, deserves special recognition. His dedication to providing outstanding service was truly remarkable. He anticipated our needs before we even voiced them, offering helpful suggestions and ensuring every detail of our meal was perfect. Whether it was a specific dietary request or simply a question about the menu, Jose handled everything with grace and efficiency.

His friendly demeanor and genuine care made us feel like valued guests, not just customers. He took the time to engage with us, creating a personal connection that elevated our dining experience far beyond simply enjoying good food. Jose's attention to detail and commitment to our satisfaction were truly commendable and significantly enhanced our time at Kicks.

The bar area was another highlight, thanks to the incredible talents of Leanniand Miguel. These two bartenders are not only skilled mixologists but also fantastic hosts. They crafted delicious and perfectly balanced cocktails with flair and efficiency. What truly stood out was their ability to create a welcoming and enjoyable atmosphere at the bar. They were attentive, ensuring our drinks were always to our liking, and engaging in friendly conversation that made us feel right at home.

Leanni and Miguel clearly take pride in their work and go the extra mile to ensure every guest leaves the bar happy and satisfied. Their positive energy and dedication to customer satisfaction are truly assets to Kicks.

reviews.text: My wife and I just returned from an unforgettable stat with friends at Paradisus, and I can’t say enough good things about this place. From start to finish, everything was top-notch. The facilities are beautiful and well-maintained, and the hospitality was truly outstanding. Our concierge, Cristian, was courteous, welcoming and ensured we had an amazing stay. Last but certainly not least Martin, bartender/beach service, was incredible, cordial and always made sure that our group was taken care of.

Our bartender Martin never missed an opportunity to check on us and make sure we were well "hydrated" :) Our room was clean and comfortable.  The food was great.  10/10 vacation. We also had the T bone steak and lobster papadell. Steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare which was to our surprise because we tend to find meats overcooked in Dominican. The flavour was spot on. The pasta had rich lobster flavour and there was generous amount of lobster meat. The service was great with our waiter Yensen providing excellent service. I feel like a lot of reviews here are not from real people so I’ll add mine. We stayed here for free on a company trip so we came with no expectations. Would we return if we had to pay? Probably not. Here are our honest impressions.

This is not a 5-star resort in American sense. We stayed in the “reserve” adults-only side. The rooms were nicely appointed but smelled somewhat musty. This side does have a decent restaurant for breakfast which is a perk because the food everywhere else is almost inedible. The pools and beach loungers are also somewhat nicer here and with somewhat better service. Nowhere close to 5-star but acceptable.

Unfortunately, the food and service are pretty poor all around. I don’t expect much from an all-inclusive but here everyone does the bare minimum and food is mediocre to inedible. They also force you to book days ahead for every dinner meal which is both inconvenient and annoying. The good thing is that Uber is easy and only a couple dollars to get to the downtown area with normal restaurants. We ended up doing that a couple times.

reviews.text:
This was our first time at an all-inclusive resort in the Dominican Republic with a child, but our travel companion was a very seasoned traveller who's stated at more than a dozen different DR hotels over the years. Our overall experience was on the positive side.

Kids club / Kidsdom 5 stars
The entire team was extremely kind, nurturing and attentive. Our daughter loved going in and asked to attend even more activities once she got a taste of the kids club. There are about half a dozen activities each day in addition to the free-play in the playroom. Thank you to Janilda, Jessica, Jesus, Joanna, Lizbet and Sujeiny - we look forward to seeing you again!

Rooms 5 stars
The hotel and rooms looked recently renovated and they were kept to an immaculate standard. Bed and bedding were comfortable, but not the sofa bed.

Beach / Pool 5 stars
Well Bavaro beach is breathless and the pools immaculate. We're glad we stayed here for the quick access to both throughout the day.

Restaurants 4 stars
Main buffet was excellent, especially since we're not "buffet people", as were the Dominican and Asian restaurants. Other restaurants were just about alright. Booking process every day for a meal out 2 days in advance was annoying.

Service 3 stars
On checkout, no one asked me how my stay was -- this is a real miss for a 5 star hotel. There were some smiley workers who made sure we were doing well throughout though; I'm very grateful for those.
Here's an example of the service: One night the cleaner attempted to deliver unsolicited towels at 10pm... we were all asleep from jetlag, had plenty of towels already, but nevertheless the doorbell rang, and after a moment the door opened. I was told to put on the do-not-disturb sign for future nights even though no one should be disturbing guests at that time of night anyway.

Entertainment 2 stars
Activities during the day were hit and miss, and evening entertainment often consisted of a solo musician with spectators scattered around the hotel. I'm told that most other hotels in the area have a proper and engaging shows.

reviews.author: Santiago Reta
reviews.text:
Nice hotel, but not worth the price (not value for money).

Based on service quality, it felt more like a 3-star hotel. It shouldn’t be rated as 5-star by today’s standards.

The hotel is beautiful and the beach is great, but they need major improvements—especially in service. We arrived at 10 a.m., checked in, but didn’t get our room until after 4 p.m. (even though check-in was at 3). It felt like if we didn’t insist multiple times, the room wouldn’t have been ready at all.

The rooms were nice and looked fairly new, but cleanliness was a major issue. There were grapes under the bed when we arrived. One day they didn’t clean at all, and the rest of the days we had to call to make sure they came. We asked them to come before 1 p.m. since we were traveling with two babies who nap around that time—only 2 days they followed through. They wouldn’t replace shampoo unless you asked, and only left a tiny trash bag. We requested room service trays to be picked up, and despite saying yes, no one came—so we spent nights with leftover food in the room.

In-room dining and all restaurants/bars (we tried them all) required repeating orders multiple times. In many cases, we gave up waiting. Most staff weren’t rude, but they didn’t seem interested in helping either. Very few asked if we needed anything, and some had a bad attitude. The general rule seemed to be: no big tip up front, no good service.

Hotel rules (zones, included services, etc.) were unclear and changed depending on the staff member—and whether they were hoping for a good tip. At check-in, they barely spoke to us, let alone explained how the hotel worked, what was included, or where to go. Everything was trial and error.

Food-wise, it was mostly average. The Asian restaurant was just bad—bland rice and chicken (think hospital food), and a very awkward show (a “chef” threw plates and glasses on a guest). In general, waiters made it feel like you were asking for a favor—not what you expect from an “all inclusive” or “premium” hotel. The steakhouse and Mexican restaurants were the best, followed by the Italian (we had to ask them to reheat the food though). Nothing was really memorable. The pre-dinner bar made great drinks though. The buffet was the most consistent, although service was also poor there. We had a great dinner at Brisas, a members-only restaurant they invited us to due to the check-in issues—but it’s not part of the usual guest experience.

Between 3–6 p.m. (when the buffet closes and restaurants open), only one snack bar is available, and with a very limited menu. Room service options were narrow. The minibar was restocked quickly, though.

Facilities and activities were below par. A yoga/stretching class lasted just 27 minutes and was led by someone scrolling on their phone. The gym had old, basic machines and no nice view—just a hallway. Activity offerings were limited and poorly communicated. The spa charged more than a walk-in at any local spa.

The hotel seems focused on events or members. During our stay, there were 3 weddings, a fashion show, and several corporate events. Nothing wrong with that, except these groups clearly had priority over regular guests. If you’re not a Meliá Circle member, I wouldn’t recommend staying here. They’ll treat you like you’re staying at a discounted 3-star hotel.

Some individual staff were kind and made an effort to improve our stay, but overall service was poor—hard to highlight the exceptions.

Lastly, third-party tour companies working with the hotel were unreliable. We booked a boat trip that turned out to be totally different from what was promised. They picked us up an hour late and didn’t allow our 6-month-old onboard (despite saying it would be fine). No refund offered.

In short: we had a very nice time because the place is beautiful, but unless you’re paying for the highest-tier experience, tipping at least $100 USD a day, and/or are a Meliá member, I wouldn’t recommend it.

reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real was nothing short of spectacular! From the moment we arrived, we were surrounded by luxury, relaxation, and top-notch service.

The beach was absolutely breathtaking—soft white sand, crystal-blue water, and plenty of loungers to unwind under the sun. The pools were beautifully maintained, offering the perfect oasis for both relaxation and fun. And, of course, the drinks were fantastic—refreshing cocktails by the pool and beachside, always perfectly made.

A special shoutout to Jendry, our incredible concierge, who went above and beyond to make our stay perfect. He ensured our clothes were always laundered on time, secured all our reservations, and even surprised us with prosecco in our room—a thoughtful touch that made our experience extra special.

At the beach, Pedro was amazing! He took care of everything, from reserving our favorite chairs to keeping us stocked with fresh drinks and afternoon snacks—his attentiveness truly made our beach days unforgettable. Pedro made our vacation so special and memorable, and we are already talking about coming back and hoping to see Pedro again.

We also indulged in the spa, where the massages were simply divine—pure relaxation in a serene setting.

Overall, Paradisus Palma Real exceeded all expectations. If you’re looking for a luxurious, relaxing, and beautifully maintained resort with exceptional service, this is the place to be. We can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: Jenna MacPherson
reviews.text:
Our family had a fantastic stay at Paradisus Palma Real in Punta Cana, with just a few minor drawbacks that, if improved, would make the experience even better.

The resort itself is stunning, set right on a beautiful, well-maintained beach. The main pool is massive, and each hotel building has its own quieter pool, which we appreciated for a more relaxing experience. However, the main pool is shared between the family-friendly and adults-only sections of the resort, and by late afternoon, it was overrun with spring break revelers. This led us to retreat to the quieter pools, which thankfully were excellent alternatives.

One issue with the main pool was the lack of shaded areas and umbrellas, which made it difficult to stay outside comfortably during the hottest parts of the day. More shade options would be a great addition.

The spa was excellent, and the adult activities throughout the day were well-organized and fun. The evening entertainment was also a highlight, with a great mix of performances and events.

The absolute standout of our trip was Kidsdom, the resort’s kids’ club. It was well-organized, engaging, and a true highlight for our children. They spent a few hours there each day, coming back thrilled about the crafts they had made and the friends they had met. The staff was incredibly welcoming—engaging our kids the moment they walked in—and even greeted them by name around the resort.

A couple of small notes for families considering this resort:

The pools are quite deep (most are nearly 5 feet), which was challenging for our younger kids and even for me as a shorter adult. This led to congestion around the pool stairs, as they were one of the few shallow spots.

Providing plastic cups and plates for kids at meals would be helpful, as the condensation on glassware made them slippery, and the ceramic plates were quite heavy for little ones.

Despite the minor inconveniences, our stay was wonderful, thanks to the beautiful resort, delicious food, and—above all—the exceptional staff. Huge thanks to Johlfrey (activities coordinator), Alexandra, Stefanie, and Sujeidi at Kidsdom, and Jamie and Alba at the spa for making our experience so special. A special recognition is also due for Maria at Rum Republic who is a fantastic bartender—kind, welcoming, and truly excellent at what she does.

We would recommend Paradisus Palma Real to families looking for a beautiful, relaxing getaway with top-notch service.

reviews.author: Denis Muggeo
reviews.text:
I stayed for 6 nights, choosing The Reserve.
Concierge, Adriel, whom I thank.

Check-in.
The entrance was not pleasant.
The reservation was made by an acquaintance who worked at the property, with the balance due during the booking process.
Upon arrival, we were asked the strangest question I've ever heard: "Is the person who made the reservation here today?"
It was explained to us as company policy that if the person is not present, the same amount already paid must be paid again.
We had to request the intervention of a supervisor of the person who was welcoming us.
We never saw this supervisor because the person later returned, saying he was confused and the person was there.
We didn't know about it, but we let it go so as not to ruin our vacation with frustration.

Once check-in was complete, they took our suitcase to the room.

The soft fabric bracelet with a wooden tag that also served as a key card was convenient. The bracelet had different colors to identify the guest's "rank."

Rooms.
Clean, elegant, comfortable. We immediately felt at home.
The exclusive area, The Reserve, is practically in the adults-only zone, a few meters from the beach and below the exclusive pool.

The room also had a fully stocked mini-bar that was refilled daily at no charge.
Having so much to eat and drink meant we rarely used the mini-bar, but the refills were always made up of the products we used.

The hairdryer, however, was broken. We reported it several times and it was never replaced.
Not very nice for a woman.

Also, what's the point of having such a large TV with only a few SD channels? You might as well not have one.

Restaurants.
There are restaurants for all tastes, and we loved them all. It's difficult to rank, but without much thought, I'd say the best was Santè, exclusive to The Reserve guests and overlooking the main pool. Our least favorite was Mina, which, in our opinion, wasn't the best meat.
In hindsight, we wouldn't have chosen it for our last night, but we would have reasoned differently.
Credit goes to the staff, who also excelled here.

We didn't try Mascalzone because, as Italians, we've learned not to eat Italian food abroad—avoid it if possible—and the buffet, as we already had Santè for breakfast and lunch.

Beach.
The exclusive area at The Reserve was something we've never seen before.
Large umbrella, two practically French-style loungers with high mattresses for each umbrella. There was room for everyone; you didn't have to rush; no matter what time you arrived, you found a spot.

The only criticism here is the towel management: some guests took 6 or 8 to cover the entire bed, and after 10:00 a.m., they were practically gone.

I also didn't understand how to choose when to help a guest. Three out of six days, I found myself searching for towels and making up the bed, but I saw this being done to others.
The same goes for orders from the umbrella.

Pool.
A large pool with several hydromassage areas, stone-tiled loungers with matching tables directly in the water, and a bar with direct access from the pool where you can enjoy your drink.

Guests at The Reserve also had an exclusive pool with an exclusive bar.

Activities.
Every evening there was something fun in the main square (circus performers, live music, silent disco, DJ set, etc.).
The concierge sends out all the day's activities.

The excursions were supposed to be included as guests of The Reserve, but we only went on one because no one told us about it.
The one we did was thanks to an acquaintance who arranged it for us, and we've never seen anything else.

General note.
Families with children or infants with free access to the adults-only area, complete with strollers and diaper changes near the pool, is confusing.

reviews.text:
My stay at Paradisus Palma Real by Meliá was amazing. My oceanfront room was the perfect choice, with a spectacular view and a huge balcony where I could relax and enjoy the scenery. The room was spacious, comfortable, and spotless, thanks to the wonderful housekeeping service, which was always available and attentive.

The highlight of my stay was definitely the Kids’ Dome. Alexandra, Susu, and Jesús were incredible—friendly, attentive, and truly engaged with the kids. They didn’t just supervise; they played with them, running in the sand, flying kites, and making every moment fun. My daughters felt happy and safe, and as a parent, that meant everything.

The food experience was great. Blue Agave was our favorite, but we also enjoyed Flora, the Asian restaurant and Kanna  which had delicious options. I didn’t try the Italian restaurant, so I can’t comment on it. The only minor issue was that service at the restaurants was a bit slow, but given that it was Spring Break and the hotel was full, it was understandable.

Evenings at the plaza were fantastic, with live music and entertainment for all ages. Instead of going to bed after dinner like we usually do on vacation, we stayed out dancing and enjoying the beautiful weather until late at night.

This hotel is perfect for families with kids, offering an excellent balance of relaxation and fun. There’s also an adults-only section for those looking for a quieter experience. Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Joe Oliveiro
reviews.text:
I'm sharing my experience with this hotel. I would highly recommend against staying here.

I am writing to express my deep disappointment and frustration with the treatment I received from your nighttime supervisor, Samson, during my recent stay at Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort. What should have been a memorable and pleasant experience was completely ruined by his unprofessionalism and lack of customer service.
To provide some context, I paid for an upgrade to my room to enhance my experience at your hotel. Part of this experience was meant to include my girlfriend spending the night with me, making my last evening truly special, as she was staying at a different hotel in Punta Cana with her family.

Prior to this incident, I spoke with my butler about bringing my girlfriend to spend the night. He informed me that it was possible but that I should confirm with the front desk. On March 21, I visited the front desk and was assured that my girlfriend could join me at any time as long as she was registered upon arrival for an additional fee of $135. I made it clear that this was not an issue, and I planned my evening accordingly.

When we arrived at the security gate, we were told that we needed to wait for permission to enter, which they said would take about five minutes. After waiting for 30 minutes, Samson, the nighttime supervisor, came out and outright refused to let us in, stating that he would not allow her to be registered. I tried to explain that I had received prior approval from the front desk and that I was fully prepared to pay the registration fee. His response was dismissive and unprofessional, stating that he was the supervisor and made the decisions.

I attempted to convey how important this evening was to me and how deeply disappointing it was to have our plans disrupted in such a manner. Instead of listening or trying to resolve the situation, he remained indifferent and continued to refuse entry. His lack of empathy and unwillingness to even consider my explanation was appalling.
What makes this experience even worse is that when I returned to the hotel alone to find out his name, he refused to properly identify himself. He mumbled his name so quickly and quietly that I could not understand him. I had to ask another staff member to confirm his name.

This entire experience was deeply upsetting and has left me with a very negative impression of what was otherwise a pleasant stay. The fact that I paid for an upgraded room and was assured that my girlfriend could be registered only to be treated so poorly is unacceptable.

I expect this matter to be taken seriously. This is not the level of service one expects from a hotel of your reputation and caliber. At the very least, I would appreciate an apology and a clear explanation of why your staff was not aligned on this policy.
I look forward to your prompt response and to hearing how you intend to address this matter.
Sincerely,

reviews.text:
My experience at Paradisus was nothing short of amazing, and the beach service truly stood out. From the moment we arrived, Marileisy & Rosanna went above and beyond to ensure we had everything we needed for a perfect day by the ocean.

The team was attentive, friendly, and always ready with a smile. Whether it was setting up our loungers in the perfect spot, bringing refreshing drinks right to our chairs, or offering delicious snacks, every detail was handled with care. The service was prompt without being intrusive, allowing us to relax and soak in the stunning views.

One highlight was the handcrafted cocktails—fresh, flavorful, and expertly made. The staff also made great recommendations and even surprised us with special treats throughout the day.

If you’re looking for a luxurious and stress-free beach experience, Paradisus delivers in every way. I can’t wait to return!

reviews.author: John Duraes
reviews.text:
We stayed the third week of March 2025 at the Paradisus Palma Real adults, only side of the hotel.
When we arrived the reception staff quickly got us checked in, served us champagne and made us feel comfortable. We were escorted to the restaurant while we waited for the room to be ready at 3 PM. They kept us updated on when the room would ready and as per the literature, we were in our room by 3:15pm.
The room was spacious, well appointed, the mini fridge well stocked. The room was always kept very clean by the housekeeping. Idelsy, our Housekeeper was wonderful, she turned down the beds at night left chocolate on a pillow, outstanding service.

Our room, overlook the beach, beautiful crystal blue waters, beautiful raked sand, and with plenty of available large, thick mattress, lounge chairs. The beach  staff were always friendly and ready to get what we needed.

Every member of the food service staff that we met were very cordial and kind to us. As we got known them, we feel like we are leaving behind a group of friends that really cared about us. They work very hard to make our vacation super enjoyable.

Compliments to the Chefs and the cooking staff. We had many excellent meals. The steaks and sea food were extremely well prepared and were excellent.

Compliments to the various bartenders and waitresses throughout out the hotel.

A special mention to Irvin, our Concierge. After our first meeting and throughout the week he was always available. He would meet us when we had breakfast and shared the day’s events. Some how he would find us at various times of day to check on us. He would schedule our events from golf tee times to parasailing to booking hairdresser appointments, restaurant reservations, etc. Thank you Irvin!!!!

Apologies if have spelled their name and or title.
Just to name a few of the staff:
* Hipólito - Assistant Manager

reviews.text:
I am leaving my original posting below the line for reference. We had a few individuals who made our stay substantially better; it is my hope that Melia management can read this and know these individuals were a substantial reason we had a positive experience. First was Betzi. He was great at helping solve some of the restaurant reservation struggles we had on our visit. Though the technology issues we encountered persisted, he at least got us in front of the Customer Service Manager and we at least we felt heard.

The second individual was Yuderqui (aka Judy). Judy waited on us at the buffet a number of times and really should be a walking icon of customer service. Our first interaction, she pushed me to practice my Spanish and was equally interested in expanding her English skills. It feels odd to say, but we felt cared for and safe with Judy. Multiple times we saw people having conversations with her and found many of us had a great fondness of her way of interacting with us. Others in this area were similar, in my experience Judy was just above and beyond. Generally I do not like many people (it is just a me thing), but I found myself having some tears over saying goodbye.

I still feel the restaurant reservation system and technology needs fixed; however this was definitely a top vacation for us. I raised this to a four star review from three really because the employees we interacted with the most went above and beyond to make our visit better. Judy and Betzi stand out by name, but there are others from the bartenders to other staff at the buffet who work hard not only to get the job done, but make you feel a touch special.
_______________
I am really struggling with this review. We generally love the resort. Our room (5016) and pool access is fantastic! The cleanliness and staff attentiveness is generally fantastic as well. However we have had smaller issues that are compounding and leaving a sour taste with two days left in our trip.

The first is the technology which is poor on a number of fronts. A couple examples, the app on my phone recognizes we are checked in and reflects the room number, however will not allow access to any menus or application capabilities while onsite. I just keep getting popup errors. So my wife tried to order room service via a phone in the room, and the people on the other end neither knew where we were calling from nor could recognize where we were located when we told them. This is not a deal breaker, but frustrating at best and so room service has been unusable for us.

The bigger challenge we have had is that restaurant reservations seem impossible to make. People seem to figure it out, but we have gotten the runaround since arriving on Tuesday. We finally had reservations last night with a reservation card; however when the card was issued they listed the wrong room number (5106 instead of 5016) and since it did not match our actual room number they would not let us in. The buffet is fine, but we spent about $4000 for five nights and have only the buffet to show for it.

This morning I hit a breaking point when seated in a corner at the buffet. I finally grabbed my daughter and just relocated ourselves to a better table with a view. It stinks being a jerk, but I feel a bit stepped on and used in the dining situation for the amount of money spent on this trip. The buffet wait staff are good and this doesn't reflect on them. They tried to make it right, I just feel pushed around a bit and they received the brunt of the restaurant reservation system. The individuals taking reservations have been unhelpful and unempathetic to the situation. There is definitely a service shortfall in this area.

Without fixing those basics I can't see recommending the Paradisus Palma Real. As a luxury resort, those are not issues guests should experience. I will update this after our trip, but as of right now am not as happy as I expect at the price point.

Unfortunately, the overall service throughout the entire place, with a few exceptions, is very poor. In the restaurants, the food preparation and quality are terrible. The only redeeming features are the facilities and the Flora restaurant; the service there is good (we were served by Melina). The restaurant's theme is Dominican and fusion cuisine.

The perception is that, since most of the tourists visiting the place are not American, the initial attention and service will not be the best. Although the hotel claims that tips are already included, it's practically a requirement to leave a tip, preferably in dollars, because even Dominican pesos are poorly received, and this is noticeable from the moment you arrive at the hotel until you leave. In short, if you don't make it clear that you will tip, you'll be practically invisible in this place.

On the other hand, it is very uncomfortable that, being a HIGH-CATE HOTEL, at any moment someone approaches you, whether it's the person who gives you the towels, walking around the facilities, or even when booking something at a themed restaurant; at all times they want to sell you some service or activity. It is truly uncomfortable and pathetic.

Here’s how to make a sandwich:

1. Gather all the ingredients you need for your sandwich. Lay them out on a clean surface such as your kitchen counter or island.
2. Take two slices of bread. You can use white, whole wheat, multi-grain, or any type you prefer.
3. On one or both slices of bread, spread your desired condiments. Common choices include mayonnaise, mustard, butter, or ketchup. You can also get creative with other spreads.
4. Add vegetables of your choice on one of the bread slices.
5. Add your chosen meat if you want to have a non-vegetarian bite. You can use 2-4 slices, depending on your preference. Overlapping them evenly on the bread works well.
6. To add creaminess and extra flavour, you can add your preferred type of cheese.
7. If you like, you can cut your sandwich in half diagonally for a classic presentation. Or use an electric sandwich maker or grill to make it more delicious.

Here, Otium Tour scammed us.

Don't let them ruin your trip like they did ours.

It's the Otium travel agency, located on the first floor of the Paradisus Hotel.

(A total of 5 people filed complaints).

Explanation: We had clearly made a reservation, but they told us it wasn't registered. Even when we showed them the booking confirmation, they claimed the information was incorrect. We finally managed to prove our reservation, but then they suddenly told us the tour was canceled and we couldn't go. They also pressured us to book a more expensive tour.

They take no responsibility whatsoever.
If you can, book your trip with an agency that guarantees confirmation of its services.

reviews.author: Trevor Kondra
reviews.text:
During our visit to the Dominican Republic, we had the pleasure of dining at an incredible buffet that truly exceeded our expectations — not just because of the delicious food, but because of the outstanding service.

Rosanna, Santo, and Yanira made our experience unforgettable. From the moment we arrived, they welcomed us with warm smiles and genuine hospitality, making us feel like family. They were attentive, friendly, and went above and beyond to ensure we were comfortable and happy throughout our meal. Whether it was recommending dishes, checking in on us regularly, or simply sharing kind words, their positive energy made all the difference.

The buffet itself was impressive, offering a wide variety of fresh, flavorful options — from local Dominican favorites to international cuisine — all beautifully presented and cooked to perfection. But what stood out even more was the way Rosanna, Santo, and Yanira made the atmosphere feel vibrant and joyful.

If you’re ever in the Dominican and looking for a place to enjoy great food paired with exceptional service, this buffet is a must-visit. Thanks to these three wonderful staff members, our meal wasn’t just satisfying — it was an experience we’ll remember for a long time.

reviews.text: Our trip was incredible thanks to the attention of Raul Jimenez, Vanessa Donastor, Joel Valdez, and Santo. Thank you for looking after us. You are the ones who made the experience so special.

reviews.author: Kristen Maurer
reviews.text:
Not the luxury arrival you would expect no towel no drink and then to make matters work we were  not given or told about resort just given incorrect information about the restaurant situation.
We were told restaurants were open or available to us when they were not open.we complained to the concierge regarding the amount of time and inconvenience we had making reservations.  The concierge told us that he would look into it and get back to us.  We never received further communication from him.
If you have a food allergy stay away I have a lactose allergy.  This was on the reservations card and was told to the staff when we arrived at the restaurant.  When questioned about the food, staff did not know what foods had lactose and at Flora I was given butter in her main dish.  I do want to point out that at Mascalzone the staff did pay attention to my food allergy.

At 11:00 am we were lying out by the adult pool.  However, our peaceful morning was interrupted by staff doing yard maintenance including using a very loud chainsaw.
Children were always in the adult area and pool. This is not enforced at all. Screaming babies and children jumping in the pool.

Every morning when we would go out to lay by the pool at 10:00 am we could not find beach towels.  We always had to wait for them.
We would ask Staff how and where to make reservations, get towels, or how to make our airport transfer. We were provided with different answers or staff didn’t know. This was frustrating because we did not know what was going on.
Staff did not explain what they were doing with our luggage during the checkout process. ie where to go, cutting wrist band, room charges.

I asked when they can cut off the wrist band she stated upon departure no one ever cut anything off of us. Another stupid thing but they all start to add up.

WiFi password was not given to us nor was there information in the room. I called and was given the information to use a certain network that didn’t work and so they said “ooo you have an apple phone, you need to to use this other network and the password was like 1000 characters and numbers. Again no information shared and when it was shared it was complicated for no reason.

Our experience at this resort was a 10 out of 10. From arrival to departure, it was unforgettable. Highly recommended!!

We enjoyed the offsite yoga experience, thanks to Jairo for being so attentive to us. And a 10 out of 10 for Amy, our instructor!!!

Regarding the themed restaurants, all of them are highly recommended. Our favorite was Mina. Special mention to Milton at Mascalzone and to Glenny and Kevin at the Japanese restaurant!!!!

A shout-out to each and every bar at the resort:
Between and Rum Republic, where Miguel and Rubi made us the best Margaritas in the Dominican Republic. Thanks to Juan Vivente for his Hemingways, made with so much love.

Ginger: A huge thank you to Anthony and Ismael for their pre-workout coffees.

And a super 10 for Luis Alejandro, Luis Rosario, and Walquiria, who made our live music nights unforgettable.

We hope to return to our home in the Dominican Republic very soon! M&P

We enjoyed an unparalleled atmosphere, with the best cocktails, a place that redefines what it means to have a good time. An unforgettable experience!"

reviews.author: Kristina khol
reviews.text:
2nd time here unfortunately my last.
Few years back I stayed as a reserve member
This time I had my reservation pre booked for me and was just at the adults only section without any reserve upgrades . Upon checkin we asked what kind of room it was I mentioned I’m here on holiday with my father .
My room was not cleaned daily till 3 pm. On first night I showed the lady the bed came without a blanket to please bring one .
I called and asked for a blanket 3 times and never got one.
The arrangement of the rooms is very unusual. There is a see through curtain with minimal to no privacy to change or while using the shower /bathroom . The see through Curtain  leaves you no privacy to change with another person in the same room accept for the tiny toilet . The shower doors are clear again no privacy . I had to hang a towel off the shower door.the coffee machine did not work.
The light stand beside the mini bar was standing for props the plug didn’t even fit into the wall socket. Strange thing to have knowing it doesn’t fit there .

They used to have a very nice spa maybe it’s on the reserve side not sure . Now the yihi spa is a hut it’s just a space for massage that they up charge $200 .

The food was a bust!
Every restaurant we went to was worse than the the last.  The sushi at Asian was terrible.
Italian was a complete fail. Served us spaghetti with clams minus the clams .
The buffet was very good . We should have stuck to that one for dinner  . We had buffet for breakfast and lunch and everything was pretty good. Not sure why the restaurants were not. The service at the restaurants was good . Same for the buffet . Water plenty of it . And the snack bar was a nice touch in the room .

The night time was weak and boring. 3 nights in a row they had some sort of meticore band playing in the lobby . Put me to sleep that I couldn’t stand to see if anything else was going on past 9:30.
Some entertainment or show would have been good but they had nothing going on.
At the beach we layed out under the umbrella had a nice relaxing time
The second day we walked out a bit and found a much more comfortable bed with mattress padding just 2 feet over from where we were yesterday. I had 3 people come to attack us that my bracelet was not Reserve and I couldn’t be there . I get the reserve privileges but did i really need the attitude to tell me to move off the mattress padded lounge chair because my bracelt was of the different color.  I paid to be on that beach too.
Anyway not sure if I lost out by not getting reserve or they just added on stupid perks for reserve members I certainly didn’t appreciate and would not come back just to get a comfier lounge chair.
Otherwise the place is beautiful has a lot of changes since I’ve been there first time . WiFi works well. Totally lacks evening entertainment.

reviews.text: Paradisus Palma Real is a beautiful resort with stunning views.  Lots of friendly staff- always willing and assist. Very clean rooms, variety of restaurants with great cuisine. reviews.author: Michael Gifford
reviews.text:
Went for 2 weeks to celebrate wife's 50th bday.  Couldn't of asked for a better trip.  The staff are extremely friendly and courteous.
Eriol our concierge went out of his way to make sure we had what we needed.  He also made our dinner reservations which was a plus.  Checked in daily to see how we were doing and loves his job.
The bartenders at all the Celcius bars are awesome.  They remember you and what you like and are always happy and dancing and having fun.
The food at every restaurant was outstanding with lots of choices.  Something for everyone.  Starting with the hostesses who were very sweet to our servers not one bad thing to say.
The grounds are immaculate and the beach is groomed constantly to keep seaweed away.
If you read any negative reviews take them with a grain of salt.  This place is the real deal.

reviews.author: Constantino Quero
reviews.text:
Spectacular 5-star luxury all-inclusive hotel with 11 pools and super attentive staff who go the extra mile to ensure you have an incredible time. Special mention to Flora, Samaria, and, of course, Laura, the hostess at the Blue Agave restaurant. All of them were very attentive and definitely enhanced our experience.

The food in the restaurants is exquisite, although you should book in advance or you won't be left without a spot. The relaxation areas are dreamy, and the rooms have beautiful views. There's so much to do that sometimes you can't decide; it's huge.

reviews.author: Diana Pukhovich
reviews.text:
KIDSDOM: Absolutely Exceptional – A Must for Families!

Our experience at Kidsdom in Paradisus Palma was nothing short of incredible! From the moment our children stepped in, they were welcomed with warmth, enthusiasm, and genuine care. The staff at Kidsdom go above and beyond to make every child feel special, all the ladies who work here (Lisbeth, Luisa, Jessica, Masiel, Sugedy whom we had the pleasure of this week) are truly the heart of it all. Their kindness, patience, and energy are unmatched—they dont just supervise the children; they engage with them, play alongside them, and make every activity exciting and memorable.

Each day was packed with fun and creative activities, from arts and crafts, cookie and pizza making, and painting to keychain designing, T-shirt making, and pool games. They even hosted special celebrations for the Dominican Independence Day, adding a cultural touch to the experience. What impressed us the most was the personal attention given to every child. The staff remember each child by name, greet them with smiles and hugs, and genuinely make them feel like part of a big, loving family.

Our kids were so happy that they would often run over just to say hello and give hugs in between activities—a true testament to how much they adored the staff and felt at home. As parents, nothing is more comforting than knowing your children are in such caring and capable hands.

If you’re visiting Paradisus Palma with kids, Kidsdom is an absolute must! It’s a safe, engaging, and magical place where children can learn, create, and have endless fun. We are beyond grateful for the love and dedication of the Kidsdom team! Thank you!

This was probably the worst experience I’ve had at an all-inclusive. I’ve stayed at Melia hotels in Spain and Italy and always received amazing service and hospitality however this was not the case with their Punta Cana resort.

I booked an oceanfront suite that would lead us right into the beach for our anniversary. They put us in the wrong room, a junior suite instead of the regular suite. When I told our “VIP concierge” he said he would look into it and after I followed up with him twice he had no answer for me.

We couldn’t get reservations for any of the restaurants even though we had our “VIP concierge” since we booked at the reserve.

The service was horrible. I had to get up and get water for ourselves when we were seated at a table for over 30 minutes. Then on another occasion we had been sitting and no one brought us utensils and I had to take them from another empty table. The buffet was bland and the food looked like it had been sitting there for hours.

It is the absolute last time I will ever visit this resort or any of the Melia Punta Cana resorts. Horrible experience.

A Truly Unforgettable Experience!

Paradisos Palma Real is nothing short of spectacular. I visited with my two boys, and from the moment we arrived, everything exceeded expectations. The resort itself is stunning, with incredible facilities, breathtaking views, and one of the most beautiful beaches in the world.

The dining experience here is phenomenal—every meal was amazing, and the variety of cuisine was impressive. The bars are equally outstanding, offering top-shelf liquor without hesitation. Nothing is held back from making your experience first-class all the way.

A special shoutout to Adriana at the Gin Ger Bar—she makes the best espresso martini I’ve ever had, and I’ve tried them all over Manhattan! If you visit, do yourself a favor and stop by to see her. You won’t be disappointed.

This resort delivers on every level, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for an all-inclusive getaway.

I love this hotel so much—this is my third time in Punta Cana, and my second time staying at the Paradisus Palma Real. After the renovation, the hotel is gorgeous, the beach is as spectacular as ever, and the rooms are always perfectly clean and incredibly comfortable.

I think this hotel also stands out for the incredible friendliness of everyone who works here. I want to especially mention the staff at the Rum Republic bar, Miguel and Yeimi, who are always attentive, friendly, and truly delightful. And they make the best drinks! Also, Yuderquis from the Lunchbox buffet was very kind, always greeting us with a smile and the best attitude!

In addition, since we came with our children, we spent a lot of time with the Kidsdom staff. They were all excellent at taking care of our children, kind and loving, and motivating them to participate in countless activities that they clearly planned with great care. Su, Alexandra, Yesica, Luisa, and Martha, among others, are truly caring and ensure that both children and parents can enjoy their days and activities at the hotel. The kids' club area is spacious and safe, perfect for children between approximately 1 and 13 years old.

All the hotel facilities are fantastic: the beach, pools, and restaurants. We love it and will definitely return, because it's also by far the most beautiful beach in the Dominican Republic. Thank you for everything!
